articles.body:
This page contains the walkthrough for Vintner's Contract: Chuchote Cave , a side quest in The Witcher 3 's Blood and Wine expansion. It's one of five Vintner's Contract missions.

Want to complete all of the Vintner's Contract quests? Check out our guides below:

You can start this side quest by traveling to Chuchote Cave, southwest of Castel Ravello Vineyard in the west of Beauclair. Here, you'll find a wine merchant outside of the cave, calling for you.

After talking to the wine merchant, you will learn he wants to use it as storage. You can haggle over the reward with him before continuing.

Head inside the cave and kill all the Arachnomorph spiders. These Arachnomorph aren't very strong, but if you're struggling (or underleveled), these monsters are weak to Insectoid Oil, as well as Aard and Axii signs.

Return and talk to the wine merchant to complete the quest and earn your pay. Additionally, the merchant will sell a variety of handy items at a discount, including alchemy ingredients, runestones, and glyphs.

articles.title: Every Secret Lair Drop - Magic: The Gathering Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Secret Lair drops are exclusive limited-time edition bundles of alternate and exclusive art treatments of preexisting Magic: The Gathering cards, and even new
articles.body:
Secret Lair drops are exclusive limited-time edition bundles of alternate and exclusive art treatments of preexisting Magic: The Gathering cards , and even new cards in some rarer cases. They're comprised of anywhere from three to eight cards, and follow a bespoke theme for each drop. Majority of drops are printed as limited runs, so they sell out fast and you'll likely be killing time in an online waiting room to get one.

Secret Lair drops have historically been comprised of artist spotlights, fun meme prints of cards, alternate art Universes Beyond cards, or premium versions of other in-Universe cards. Secret Lair is also where Universes Beyond got its start, with the Walking Dead drop in October of 2020.

You can also find Mood Swings on Secret Lair, a new simplified card from Magic head designer Mark Rosewater.

First and foremost, it's worth it to try and purchase Secret Lair drops directly from the Secret Lair store . That way, you know you're getting a new, unopened product, as well as paying the MSRP price. There are even a handful of Secret Lair drops available to buy on Amazon , but they're few and far between - and some are sold and shipped by a third party instead of Amazon itself.

Secondary online cards storefronts are where most people will buy either their sealed Secret Lair drops, or peruse the single cards they want instead of the full package. TCG Player is the world's most prominent online card shop, but Card Kingdom is another great option. You can also find Secret Lair drops on eBay .

Both retailers have knocked its standard edition down to $60.99, saving you $9 off its original cost. It may be a minor price cut, but for a game we consider to be among the best of the year so far , it's certainly still worth looking into.

With that kind of praise, it's hard to resist grabbing it for your gaming library, especially while it has a few bucks knocked off its list price.

As we get further into November, more video game deals like this are sure to pop up in Black Friday sales. Some retailers are even kicking off the seasonal sale celebrations early this year, like Target and Best Buy . Each retailer's timing is a bit different, though. If you're curious when the official Black Friday sales begin this year, have a look at our write-up of Black Friday 2026 for a rundown of sale start dates for different retailers alongside some of our deal predictions for this year.

articles.title: Nintendo says it’s not planning another Switch 2 price hike
articles.summary: Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa said during an earnings call that it’s not considering another price change for the Switch 2, according to Reuters.
articles.body: Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa said during the company’s latest earnings call that it’s “not considering additional changes” to the Switch 2’s price, Reuters reports. The Switch 2 got a $50 price hike earlier this year, bringing its starting price up to $499. Nintendo said in Thursday’s earnings report that Switch 2 sales have dropped 37.4 percent year-over-year. According to Reuters, Furukawa also gave an update on the RAM shortage, saying, “There has been no major change to the memory situation and Nintendo is in a position to secure sufficient quantities.” Earlier this week, one of Nintendo’s Switch 2 cartridge suppliers announced it plans to stop making ROM memory to focus on memory for data centers instead. Demand from AI data centers is driving the ongoing RAM shortages that’s leading to a wave of tech price increases. Microsoft has raised Xbox Series X / S prices multiple times now, increasing the Series S’s starting price from $299 to $499. The PS5 has also been hit with price hikes, taking its starting price up to $649.

articles.title: World of Warcraft Forever's Launch Was Running on Over 200,000 Gigabytes of RAM
articles.summary: World of Warcraft Forever launched last night, and while there were a ton of people playing, the servers were remarkably stable. And, it turns out that Blizzard dedicated a ton of resources to making those servers stable.
articles.body:
World of Warcraft Forever launched last night, and while there were a ton of people playing, the servers were remarkably stable . It turns out that Blizzard dedicated a ton of resources to making sure those servers were solid.

Last night, after the game launched, Blizzard tweeted out a meme from its World of Warcraft account, with a Gnome tapping a car with the WoW Forever logo, with a caption saying: "*Slaps Roof of WoW: Forever* This baby is running on: 3,924 Virtual Machines, 251,136 GB of Memory, 70,480 CPU Cores." That's a huge amount of memory, and it seems to have paid off with the smoothest Blizzard launch I've seen in years.

Blizzard's post bragging about the sheer amount of memory in its servers comes just a week after Sam Altman said in a podcast that it was "quite terrible" for people to have RAM in their own computers, rather than in a data center. Of course, he did later walk it back , instead claiming that he had "been arguing for the world to ramp up memory production for a long time." Still, that's 251,136GB of RAM that's dedicated to running an incredible MMO, rather than powering yet another data center.

*Slaps Roof of WoW: Forever* This baby is running on: 3,924 Virtual Machines 251,136 GB of Memory 70,480 CPU Cores — World of Warcraft (@Warcraft) November 5, 2026

*Slaps Roof of WoW: Forever* This baby is running on: 3,924 Virtual Machines 251,136 GB of Memory 70,480 CPU Cores

Blizzard Executive Producer and Vice President for World of Warcraft Holly Longdale also posted celebrating the smooth launch, and said "this launch was crazier than the insanity we imagined but thankfully the team built plans and contingencies. They are incredible imo." And, while we likely will never know just how many people logged into Forever for the launch, I can say firsthand that there were hundreds of characters in the starting zone right at 6pm EST, so the team definitely deserves recognition for holding everything together.

Even on the WoW forums, which are hardly a bastion of positivity, there are a number of threads with players praising WoW Forever for being one of the smoothest WoW launches of all time . On X/Twitter, WoW streamer Darth Microtransaction posted, "I don’t know how they did it, but they did. World of Warcraft Forever launch was the smoothest launch I’ve seen. Almost 0 Que[ue]. 0 dc, and no lag."

This launch was a solid start to a game that's going to take most people weeks to go through. The beta was huge on its own, despite being limited to just level 30. And, even when folks knew their characters would get deleted, so many people played the beta that developers commented on it for being the "craziest numbers [they've] seen." And now that the full game is here, it's going to be interesting to see what players discover, and what gets added in the future. Because, according to Blizzard, there's potential to visit some fan favorite locations from future expansions , too.

articles.title: Rapper Kodak Black Will Be an NPC in GTA 6, Creating Speculation Over Other Artists Appearing In-Game
articles.summary: Rapper Kodak Black has been confirmed to be featured as an NPC in GTA 6 via a new batch of screenshots.
articles.body:
Rapper Kodak Black has been confirmed to be featured as an NPC in GTA 6 via a new batch of screenshots.

Rockstar Games released a batch of 39 new screenshots from GTA 6 to celebrate the game being two weeks away from launch, and one of them reveals that Kodak Black will be in the game. Upon closer examination, we can see him holding a cup with the Jack of Hearts logo, which is a club in GTA 6. This club has appeared in various marketing beats for the game, and Travis Scott even name-dropped it in his song, RHYNO, which was made specifically for GTA 6's soundtrack.

It has been heavily speculated that this club would feature a variety of real-world artists, and the confirmation of Kodak Black seems to only add fuel to that speculation. It doesn't seem like a leap to imagine that other artists like Scott or other rappers featured on the game's soundtrack could also appear in-game. There's some precedent for this in previous GTA titles, too.

In GTA Online, Dr Dre appeared as a character that the player could do missions for. The game's nightclubs also featured real DJs such as Solomun, Tale of Us, and Dixon, so it's entirely possible Rockstar managed to get these artists to do real performances at clubs in the game. We'll ultimately have to wait and see, but it's clear that Rockstar has spared no expense with the talent for this game. While there will be some fresh faces in the cast, actor Stephen Root confirmed earlier this year that he will play Brian Heder in GTA 6. The character is expected to be Jason's boss and a drug runner.

Some of the game's radio stations are also hosted by the likes of Lana Del Rey, Bad Bunny, Morgan Wallen, and other major musicians and celebrities. There may be other celebrity cameos in GTA 6, but Rockstar is trying to keep a veil of secrecy around the entire game to preserve the experience for launch.

Speaking of launch, Rockstar Games confirmed earlier this week that pre-loading for GTA 6 will begin on November 10 . The game will take up around 212 GBs of space on your storage device, so you may want to go clear some space for this behemoth so you have all the time needed to prepare for launch.

articles.title: Pokémon Cards Get Official Induction Into National Toy Hall of Fame
articles.summary: The National Toy Hall of Fame has officially announced this year’s inductees, and the biggest TCG of all time has finally made the cut.
articles.body:
The National Toy Hall of Fame has officially announced this year’s inductees, and one of the biggest trading card games of all time has finally made the cut.

Pokémon cards were inducted into the Toy Hall of Fame on the morning of Thursday, November 5, as the franchise celebrates its 30th anniversary. Other new additions from this year’s lineup include Bingo, Care Bears, and the classic slide, which beat out nominees like Bop It!, mahjong, and Polly Pocket.

"Pokémon TCG’s widespread appeal and global presence are undeniable," said curator Mirek Stolee. "The Pokémon TCG successfully adapted card game formulas established by its predecessors, making it more accessible and infusing it with the lovable Pokémon creatures."

The National Toy Hall of Fame was established in 1998 to "recognize toys that have inspired creative play and enjoyed popularity over a sustained period." The Hall of Fame is currently housed at the Strong Museum of Play in Rochester, New York, which is also home to the World Video Game Hall of Fame.

Anyone can nominate a toy for consideration. A panel of museum curators, historians, and educators then evaluate these nominees based on four pillars: icon status, longevity, discovery, and innovation. The Hall of Fame has a relatively loose definition of a toy, having previously inducted a cardboard box and the concept of 'sand' in addition to classics like LEGO, Barbies, and slinkies.

This isn’t the first time a trading card game has made it onto the prestigious toy list. Magic: The Gathering was added in 2019, nearly 10 years after the induction of another tabletop classic, Dungeons & Dragons .

The Strong website now has a section dedicated to the Pokémon TCG , where it describes the game’s history and cultural impact:

"[Pokémon TCG] has played a pivotal role in popularizing the concept of trading card games and has served as an entryway into the hobby for millions. The Pokémon TCG has even spawned its own video game (for Game Boy) and app (available on multiple platforms), thus completing the circle back to its video game origins. Recently, the cards have become the focus of major financial speculation. Online viewers watch content creators “rip,” or open, TCG packs, in the hope of finding valuable, rare cards."

As of March 2026, more than 85 billion Pokémon cards have been printed and distributed globally. The trading card game is currently being printed in 13 different languages, and rough estimates put the total market cap above $15 billion.

As the museum description implies, however, the massive explosion of Pokémon’s popularity hasn’t really been a good thing for most fans. Scalping has plagued the community for years now, turning the once casual card game hobby into a collector’s racket. Market prices have soared out of control , threatening the 'accessibility' the Toy Hall of Fame specifically praises the game for.

The Pokémon Company is aware of the problem, and has repeatedly announced its intentions to increase stock to combat it. This increased production seems to have taken effect with the recent 30th anniversary product line, which led to scalpers complaining the set isn't profitable enough.

As for the Hall of Fame, Pokémon’s induction will likely lead to new exhibits and events at The Strong in the new year.

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

Speaking of items, when you play as Survivor, you'll start the game with a Lantern .

When you're holding the Lantern, you'll be able to see the auras of Pallets and Windows (sort of like the Windows of Opportunity perk).

If you use the Lantern, you'll be able to see the Generator closest to you. You can also place a Lantern on top of a Generator , so the aura of it is revealed to other survivors. This also comes in handy if you finish the Generator, because the auras of all other Generators will be blocked from being seen by the Killer.

articles.title: The SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless Gaming Headset With Infinite Battery Life Drops to a New Low
articles.summary: Snag these $350 headphones for well under $200 ahead of Black Friday.
articles.body:
One of the best wireless gaming headsets just dropped to its lowest price ever. Woot, which is owned by Amazon, is offering a new Steelseries Arctis Nova Pro wireless gaming headset for PS5, PS4, and PC for just $183.99 after you apply 20% off coupon code " PCGAMING ". Amazon Prime members get free shipping, otherwise add $5 for delivery. This is a brand new, unused headset that comes with a 90-day Woot warranty.

SteelSeries Nova Pro Wireless Gaming Headset for $184

SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless Gaming Headset (PS5, PC)

The SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro has long been one of IGN's highest rated wireless gaming headsets . IGN's Kevin Lee gave the Nova Pro a 10/10 "Masterpiece" review and I believe it still holds today. I've clocked well over a thousand hours on mine to the point that my earcups were worn through (I replaced them with the awesome WC Freeze gel earpads ). SteelSeries released a successor - the Nova Pro Omni - earlier this year, but it currently sells for $380 and the improvements are certainly not worth the nearly $200 price premium. The Omni's pièce de résistance is its seamless cross-platform switching. If you predominantly use these headphones for one platform, then stick with the Nova Pros.

The one feature that undoubtedly makes the Nova Pro stand out amongst the crowd is the ingenious hot-swappable battery system . The Nova Pro includes two removable, rechargeable batteries: one to use in your headset and the other to remain charged and ready to go in a base station that doubles as a charger. This way, you get wireless freedom with zero downtime . Each battery lasts for up to 22 hours of continued use so you don't need to swap out too often.

The base station deserves additional mention. Not only does it charge your battery, it also features a clear and legible OLED display and a handy volume control knob. On the rear are USB inputs for connecting to your PC as well as an optional 3.5mm passthrough should you want to connect your speakers directly to the base station.

Of course a high end gaming headset is no good if it can't produce great sound and deliver vocal clarity. The Nova Pro is first and foremost a gaming headset, and it delivers big sound with its big 40mm neodymium dynamic drivers and 360° spatial sound effects (via SteelSeries Sonar for PC, Tempest 3D Audio for PS5, and Microsoft Spatial Sound for Xbox). The retractable boom mic is clear without any static and does a great job of canceling out ambient noise. My friends regularly point out that I sound like I'm in a quiet room because they hear nothing but my voice.

The Nova Pro is comfortable to use even during gaming marathons thanks to the suspension-style headband and comfortable leatherette ear cushions. You don't have to worry about babying it either, since the headband has a steel inner core. I've tossed mine around more times than I should have and it's still functionally perfect.

articles.title: EA Sports retira a Jesús de Miguel de los sobres de Ultimate Team tras su fallecimiento y este es el motivo
articles.standfirst: Desde hace tiempo, EA Sports sigue esta política en este tipo de casos
articles.summary: Desde hace tiempo, EA Sports sigue esta política en este tipo de casos
articles.body: EA Sports ha tomado una decisión sobre la carta de Jesús de Miguel en Ultimate Team después del fallecimiento del futbolista del CD Tenerife tras sufrir un incidente durante su último partido. La compañía ha aplicado el procedimiento habitual en este tipo de situaciones y ha anunciado la retirada del jugador de los sobres del popular modo de juego de EA Sports FC. De esta forma, su artículo dejará de formar parte de los posibles contenidos que pueden conseguir los usuarios al abrir sobres. Sin embargo, aquellos jugadores que ya tengan su carta en el club podrán conservarla. Eso sí, pasará a ser intransferible, por lo que no podrán venderla ni utilizarla en el mercado de transferencias. La medida no ha terminado de convencer a toda la comunidad de Ultimate Team. Algunos usuarios no entienden cómo retirar a un futbolista de los sobres puede servir para honrar su memoria y consideran que la decisión resulta contradictoria. Sin embargo, detrás de este procedimiento hay un motivo importante. EA Sports busca impedir que algunos jugadores aprovechen el fallecimiento de un futbolista para especular con su carta, aumentar su precio en el mercado y conseguir monedas a costa de una tragedia. Por ese motivo, la compañía no se limita a retirar estos artículos de los sobres, sino que también modifica las cartas que ya están en circulación. Al convertirlas en intransferibles, elimina la posibilidad de que los usuarios puedan venderlas y sacar partido de una eventual subida de su valor. Aunque pueda parecer una medida reciente, lo cierto es que EA Sports lleva varios años aplicando este tipo de decisiones. El procedimiento actual tiene su origen en lo ocurrido tras el fallecimiento de Emiliano Sala en enero de 2019. En aquel momento, la compañía retiró al futbolista argentino de los sobres de FIFA y limitó el rango de precios de su carta en el mercado de transferencias. Sin embargo, estas restricciones no fueron suficientes para evitar que algunos usuarios intentaran aprovecharse de la situación y elevar su valor todo lo posible. A raíz de aquello, EA decidió adoptar un procedimiento más estricto para este tipo de casos: retirar las cartas de los sobres y convertir en intransferibles aquellas que ya se encuentran en las plantillas de los jugadores. De esta manera, la compañía pretende evitar cualquier tipo de especulación y que nadie pueda obtener monedas aprovechándose del fallecimiento de un futbolista. Una medida que vuelve a aplicar ahora con Jesús de Miguel y que busca preservar el respeto hacia su memoria también dentro de Ultimate Team.

articles.title: Michael Murphy: Donegal great retires from inter-county football
articles.summary: Donegal's All-Ireland winning captain Michael Murphy retires from inter-county football, the county confirms.
articles.body:
Donegal's All-Ireland winning captain Michael Murphy has announced his retirement from inter-county football for the second time.

The 37-year-old made his Donegal debut in 2007 and captained the county to All-Ireland success in 2012, scoring 1-4 as they beat Mayo in the decider.

The Glenswilly forward also won six Ulster Senior Football titles, including back-to-back triumphs in 2018 and 2019, and is a four-time All Star.

He previously announced his inter-county retirement in 2022, but reversed the decision two years later and made a triumphant return under Jim McGuinness in the 2025 season.

He helped his county to retain the Anglo-Celt Cup with an extra-time victory against Armagh and reach the All-Ireland final, which they lost to Kerry.

His stellar performances earned him a fourth All-Star while he was also nominated for the Footballer of the Year award that year.

Murphy stayed on for the 2026 season and while Donegal won the Division One title, his last game was their All-Ireland round-three exit to Dublin in June.

"The Donegal County Board has today announced that former All-Ireland winning captain Michael Murphy has retired from inter-county football," the county said in a statement.

"The player informed management in recent weeks once the club championship had concluded.

"Michael has been Donegal's talisman for a generation and captained the county for most of his career having made his senior debut back in 2007. Two seasons ago, he came out of retirement, winning a sixth Ulster medal, his fourth All-Star and a national league title in the process."

Paying tribute to Murphy's decorated inter-county career, Donegal county board chairperson Mary Coughlan added: "Alas, we always knew this day would come but we are privileged to have watched the stellar career of Michael Murphy up close.

"What he has given Donegal GAA on-and-off the field is simply extraordinary while always an ambassador par excellence and role-model for so many young people in our county and beyond.

"He is one of the giants of the modern game and when players talk about leaving the jersey in a better place on retiring, Michael has certainly done that. He has carried himself with tremendous dignity and integrity at all times.

"His innate modesty is a foil for a fierce competitor who never gave less than 100% while inspiring others around him to do likewise."

Murphy's retirement is a further blow for boss McGuinness, who decided to remain at the helm for a fourth year in his second stint.

He has also lost talented defender Finnbarr Roarty after the 2025 Young Footballer of the Year signed a two-year rookie contract with Aussie Rules outfit Collingwood.

'Complete forward and fearless leader' - analysis

Now widely regarded as Donegal's greatest player, Murphy broke on to the senior county panel as an all-action teenager in 2007.

The esteem in which he was held, even in those early years, within the squad was reflected by McGuinness handing him the captaincy at the age of 21.

Led by the Murphy-McGuinness twin axis, Donegal were hauled out of the doldrums in 2011 when they claimed the Division Two title, with Murphy hitting 1-3 in the final win over Laois.

Later that year, he led his county to their first Ulster title in 19 years and spearheaded a successful defence 12 months later.

But his greatest moment arrived three minutes into the 2012 All-Ireland final against Mayo.

Rising high to claim Karl Lacey's long kickpass, he shook off Kevin Keane and rifled a venomous right-footed shot high into the net for one of the great championship goals - one that encapsulated Murphy's power and precision.

Aged 23, Murphy became a county legend that day, becoming just the second man after Anthony Molloy to captain Donegal to the ultimate prize. He scored 1-3 but the goal remains etched in the minds of anyone who watched it.

Murphy soldiered on with Donegal for another 10 years - collecting another three Ulster titles - before announcing his retirement in November 2022, later telling The GAA Social that fear of not having the energy to reach his usual lofty standards was a factor in his decision.

It was news that rocked Donegal, but at 33, it always felt as though Murphy could return. McGuinness' second coming in 2023 only fuelled the rumour mill.

While Murphy extended his stint as a leading analyst and co-commentator for the BBC in 2024, Donegal fans' dreams came true when he reversed his retirement before the 2025 season.

Lean, sharp and now armed with a two-point boot - thanks to the new rules he helped usher in as part of Jim Gavin's Football Review Committee - Murphy delivered another Ulster title for McGuinness.

Murphy was named man of the match on Ulster final day, but heartache followed in the All-Ireland final. Murphy scored eight points but was upstaged by another talismanic forward in David Clifford, who kicked 0-9 to drive Kerry over the line.

While a second Sam Maguire ultimately eluded Murphy, he remained clutch under pressure until the end, nailing a two-pointer on his 200th appearance to force extra-time against Dublin, although his part in the ensuing brawl earned him a black card.

It proved a bitter end to Murphy's storied Tir Chonaill career, but Donegal fans will remember him as the complete forward and fearless leader responsible for some of the county's greatest days.

articles.title: Award-Winning Duo Behind Niko and the Sword of Light Launch New Interactive Fantasy Comic
articles.summary: The award-winning duo behind Niko and the Sword of Light have launched a new interactive fantasy comic called Magrid’s Magic Shoppe.
articles.body:
Bobby Chiu and Jim Bryson, the creators of the Emmy-winning Niko and the Sword of Light , are back with Magrid’s Magic Shoppe, an interactive project billed as “the world’s first infinitely zooming playable fantasy comic” that lets readers zoom into the art to find clues and solve puzzles. The duo launched a Kickstarter to fund their latest passion project, which ends on November 6.

Built on Bryson’s hand-drawn artwork and the new interactive creator platform An Infinite Story, Magrid’s Magic Shoppe lets audiences explore the art panel by panel, uncover hidden details, find clues, and solve puzzles. Bryson describes the result as “somewhere between comics, animation and games.”

The idea grew from a childhood dream of discovering what’s hidden inside a comic page. “I can sketch out an idea for a sequence and have it working interactively within minutes,” Bryson says. “Watching a drawing develop into an experience you can explore still feels a bit like magic.”

Chiu and Bryson made history with their previous collaboration on Niko and the Sword of Light, an animated comic book app that was adapted into an animated series for Amazon Prime Video. The show was the first pilot to win an Emmy Award before the series had even premiered.

Chiu co-founded An Infinite Story and has more than 20 years experience in film, animation, and art. He worked as a character designer on Tim Burton’s Alice in Wonderland and founded LightBox Expo and Schoolism. Bryson is a founding member of StudioNX, a visual development studio whose clients include Marvel, Disney, Amazon, and Nickelodeon.

The Kickstarter campaign also serves a bigger goal. Funds will help develop An Infinite Story into a toolkit that lets independent artists turn existing artwork into interactive, monetizable experiences without programming skills or a large studio. “Artists have more ways than ever to share their work, but it’s still super hard to make a living from independent art,” Chiu says.

Rewards include digital artwork, early access to the interactive experience, physical art books, signed collectibles, original art and even the chance to be inserted into the story as an illustrated character with dialogue.

Magrid’s Magic Shoppe is on Kickstarter now.

For each of the Anniversary Editions, including my personal favorite, Road Rash (check out the trailer above), EA says, "The Anniversary Editions have been a labor of love, inspired by the discovery of a physical media vault containing thousands of Betacam, VHS, and D1 tapes alongside other media assets. The digitization process recovered the supposedly lost Master FMV sequences for these seven legendary titles, which were meticulously re-edited to restore the over 1,500 cinematic scenes across these games."

The Ultima series, meanwhile, was the brainchild of legendary RPG designer Richard "Lord British" Garriott, who went on to build a castle for a house and later become one of the first private citizens to go into outer space. You can hear about those stories and more on my old IGN Unfiltered interview with him from 2017.

Hua Qianxiao, the Sword Fanatic is a story boss in Phantom Blade Zero , and he appears during the Snake's Reflection main quest. He's the first story boss you encounter in the Crimson Forest. Here are a few tips and strategies for how to beat him.

How to Defeat Hua Qianxiao, the Sword Fanatic

Hua Qianxiao, the Sword Fanatic , is one of the men you saw Soul fighting against in the flashback at the first Crane Bell in the Crimson Forest. He’s a shifty opponent who uses water to attack. These are the special moves you need to be aware of:

Hua Qianxiao is an erratic boss who attacks using quick, multi-hit combos. You might need to see his moves a few times to get used to their speed and timing.

Focus more on defense than offense because Hua Qianxiao can hit you with his floating sword even while you’re attacking him. You’re only fully safe to counterattack after a blue-flash parry, a red-flash dodge, or when you deplete the boss’s Sha-Chi meter. But pay attention, because his meter refills quickly.

When you do break his guard, you can use Power Surges to deal the most damage, especially with Jagged Steel or the Scarlet Wraithblade

You obtain The Fanatic’s Broken Blade Main Weapon (One-Handed) after winning the fight. Its unique ability allows you to drink by pressing L1 + Triangle on controller or Right Click + F on keyboard. You can also hold the buttons/keys to drink longer.

Drinking restores Sha-Chi and makes you tipsy, which allows you to use ranged sword attacks like Hua Qianxiao. Use the Power Surge while sober to immediately enter a tipsy state. Use it when tipsy to enter the drunk state, which disables your block, enables automatic dodges, and increases damage.

The Fanatic’s Broken Blade shares upgrade materials with Jagged Steel since they’re both One-Handed weapons. You should choose one or the other to avoid splitting upgrade materials at this point. You can use a Weapon Reforge Talisman to revert Jagged Steel and transfer those upgrades to the new weapon if you want to swap.

articles.title: BioWare's Final Years Were Filmed and Will Be Revealed in a New Documentary
articles.summary: The last two years of BioWare's life were filmed and will be shown in a new documentary about the game studio.
articles.body:
The last two years of BioWare's life were filmed and will be shown in a new documentary about the game studio.

The documentary, titled Massive Effect: The BioWare Story, will show the studio's journey over the last few years. While it's unclear if this will include new footage of the canceled Mass Effect game, it is a rare peek behind the curtain and likely a raw one, given how the story ends. Industry veteran Geoff Keighley revealed that he was interviewed for the film earlier this year, and confirmed that it will be released sometime in 2027.

The project is being produced by Shane Fennessey and Adam Scorgie for Canada‘s Super Channel, as BioWare was primarily a Canadian studio. It's unclear if it will also be made available online for those outside of Canada. The documentary will feature exclusive interviews and insights from BioWare talent, such as Mass Effect game director Casey Hudson, Jennifer Hale (voice actress for the female variant of Commander Shepard), and many more. It should be an interesting watch whenever it is released.

“When the production team asked for our blessing to tell the BioWare story, we were honoured and genuinely moved,” said BioWare co-founders Dr. Ray Muzyka and Dr. Greg Zeschuk. “BioWare was never just about the logo or the building. It was about deeply emotionally engaging stories and characters, brought to life by the amazingly talented people on our dev teams, and our excellent production and distribution partners who helped us bring those stories successfully to all corners of the planet, and our passionate fans who defended those worlds, championed them and carried them forward. We’re proud this film honours those who made it all possible. The best stories never really end. They live on in our memories and wait for someone to pick them up again.”

11 Mass Effect Characters and Moments the TV Show Needs to Be a Hit

BioWare was shut down last month , much to the shock of the wider industry and fans alike. The studio had been struggling for a while; its last three games were misfires, and the next Mass Effect game was expected to still be years away. As a result, EA reportedly decided to place its bets on a new Star Wars Battlefront game from DICE and Respawn instead of continuing to fund a new Mass Effect game.

A trailer for Mass Effect 5 , which was apparently called Mass Effect Universe, did find its way online, painting a better picture of what fans could've expected from the canceled game. Some fans have held out hope that the Mass Effect IP could be acquired by another company, but as of right now, it doesn't seem like that's in the cards.

articles.body:
Stone Hand Iron Fever is a story boss in Phantom Blade Zero , and he appears during the Snake's Reflection main quest. He's the third story boss you encounter in the Crimson Forest. Here are a few tips and strategies for how to win this fight.

Climb down the ladder near the Mirrorwood Entrance bell to enter a wide clearing where you face off against Stone Hand Iron Fever .

These are the special moves you need to know about:

Iron Fever deals big damage in melee range since he attacks with his fists. Be ready to parry quick combos with no gimmicks. He just wants to punch and kick you, so try to get used to his combo timings.

Iron Fever’s weakness is that his blue-flash and red-flash attacks don’t change up very much in the first half of the fight. They often come out of the same combo, and your counters deplete huge chunks of his Sha-Chi meter, giving you plenty of time to perform long combos as he recovers.

Iron Fever becomes enraged and glows purple once his HP hits 50%. He becomes far more aggressive, but his moves stay largely the same.

He does add one new red-flash grab, though. Watch for when he pauses, then lunges straight at you as he flashes red. This one isn’t part of a combo.

Other than that, you should be a bit more defensive in this phase because his attacks come in rapid succession with very few pauses. Don’t try to counterattack too early or you’ll end up getting caught in his next combo.

You’re rewarded with the Iron Gauntlets Phantom Edge (Martial) after winning the battle. The Iron Gauntlets have high shield-breaking power and can buff your main weapon as you land hits.

articles.summary: The ending of Godzilla Minus Zero leaves just enough room for a continuation of the story filmmaker Takashi Yamazaki has crafted, but the writer/director says he's split on whether or not he'd want to come back to it.
articles.body:
Godzilla Minus Zero writer/director Takashi Yamazaki told The Hollywood Reporter that he's "fifty-fifty" on whether or not he'd come back to make a third Godzilla film.

Extremely minor Godzilla Minus Zero spoilers ahead!

"I’m quite satisfied and happy with the current ending we have," Yakazaki said when asked about the film's ambiguous ending that leaves just enough room for a continuation of the story. "It entrusts the interpretation to the audience in terms of how they want to receive it and what they want to walk out of theaters with. That being said, if Godzilla Minus Zero is my last Godzilla film, that would make me a bit sad. I do have other films lined up, starting with Grandgear and a few others, but at some point in my career, I would love to revisit Godzilla and see how we can expand this world."

Grandgear was announced in 2024 as Yamazaki's first major Hollywood studio movie, with Sony Pictures, and his first English-language feature film. It's currently slated for a February 18, 2028 release . Starring Sam Nivola (The White Lotus Season 3), Nico Parker (The Last of Us, the live-action How to Train Your Dragon), and Paul Giamatti (it's Paul Giamatti...), Grandgear is a live-action sci-fi mecha movie, something Yamazaki also told THR was "something I’ve always wanted to do." Yamazaki is writing and directing, and Bad Robot is producing.

But first, Godzilla Minus Zero comes out in U.S. theaters this weekend, a mere three years after Godzilla Minus One became a box-office sensation in 2023 on a reportedly tiny $10–15 million budget and a lean 35-person VFX team, with Yamazaki overseeing. It went on to win the Oscar for Best Visual Effects, marking the first time a Japanese film took home the award, and did it with the tiniest budget of any category winner in more than a decade .

Yamazaki told IGN that, when writing Godzilla Minus Zero, he had to set aside the need to try and one-up everything he had accomplished with Godzilla Minus One. “I think it's very dangerous to create a movie with that type of mindset because you're going to risk diluting what makes the movie great in the first place," he said. "So those are the wrong reasons to make a movie and it ends up becoming an antagonist in your moviemaking process.”

Godzilla Minus Zero is both the first R-rated Godzilla movie and the first Japanese film to be specifically shot for IMAX screens. It's also very loud ! We said it was Good in our review , calling out its "satisfying and visually amazing scenes of giant-monster destruction."

But back to the potential of a third Godzilla movie. Turning these films into a trilogy raises a critical question: What would it be called, after the naming convention has already counted down from Minus One to Minus Zero? I have a pitch: Godzilla Plus One that, of course, introduces another new kaiju. Toho, call me!

Leanne Butkovic (she/they) is an Editorial Programming Manager at IGN, where they've also written about TV, movies, and games.

articles.title: The Odyssey Is Returning to IMAX Theaters in December Ahead of Awards Season
articles.summary: The Odyssey is returning to theaters in December for one last hoorah before awards season goes into full swing.
articles.body:
The Odyssey is returning to theaters in December for one last hoorah before awards season goes into full swing.

Universal has announced that Christopher Nolan's R-rated epic will return to theaters on December 11 in over 1,000 cinemas across the United States and Canada. The film will be coming back to IMAX screens, including ones that support the 70MM IMAX format it was designed for. This is presumably part of a larger campaign to get The Odyssey some awards buzz ahead of the Oscars, and probably earn some extra pocket change for the studio.

The Odyssey has already made $1.8 billion at the box office to become the highest-grossing R-rated film in history . It seems hard to imagine this re-release getting it over the hump for $2 billion, as Dune Part 3 will take over premium format screens on December 18. Avengers: Doomsday will also take up as much attention for movie lovers, if not more. It's unclear if The Odyssey will continue to play on regular screens after those two movies are released, or if this is a limited one-week run.

The Odyssey is a favorite for many of the big prestigious awards, with many expecting a Best Picture nomination, Best Actor for Matt Damon, Best Director for Christopher Nolan, and many more. Whether it scores all of the nominations it's expected to get remains to be seen. It'll also be interesting to see what awards it could win, as Nolan's last film, Oppenheimer, cleaned house at the Oscars in 2023. It's rare for a filmmaker to win big twice in a row, though not unheard of. Alejandro González Iñárritu won Best Director back-to-back years in 2014 and 2015 for Birdman and The Revenant, respectively.

Nevertheless, it'll be a busy time at the movie theater in December with the return of The Odyssey and some of the year's heaviest hitters with Dune and Avengers. For those who aren't interested in venturing out into the cold to see Nolan's latest film again, The Odyssey is also coming to home video later this month .

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Dr. Doom Is Taking Over Dave and Buster’s in Lead-up to Avengers: Doomsday
articles.summary: Dr. Doom’s latest target is entertainment chain Dave and Buster’s, which has fully submitted to the Marvel villain for an expansive Avengers: Doomsday campaign.
articles.body:
Dr. Doom’s latest target is entertainment chain Dave and Buster’s, which has fully submitted to the Marvel villain for an expansive Avengers: Doomsday campaign.

Starting on November 16, Dave & Buster’s is becoming Doom & Buster’s. Select locations are already rolling out ‘Doomsday Zones,’ entire sections of the arcade dedicated to the Avengers takeover. Enter the Dr. Doom archway and you’ll find a collection of Marvel games and activities in addition to new D&B drinks and prizes.

"When one of the biggest movies of the year is coming, you don't put up a poster. You bend the knee," said Jeremy Tucker, chief marketing officer at Dave & Buster's. "We gave Doom our name. We gave him the floor. We gave him the bar… All shall play."

As one of the leading arcade chains, the big tie-in is games. On Dave & Buster's floors, fans can already find a new selection of Marvel-themed activities:

Cosmic Invasion is the big headliner here. The game dropped on PC and consoles last December, and through the D&B campaign, is now getting the full arcade cabinet treatment. Like the fully released version, the arcade edition will support up to four players.

We’re pretty big fans of the tag-team beat-em up, saying it "has the juice" in our 7/10 review , which knocks off some points for a limited hero gallery. Thankfully, the game has released plenty of new content in the past year. A new Doom-themed DLC, 'The Siege of Castle Doom,' is launching on November 10, and will presumably be included in the in-store activations.

New prizes vary across locations. The crane games are packed with their own range of Marvel-specific collectibles, including some vaguely described "new inflatables." Doomsday Zones will also feature a fully stocked Avengers Funko pusher, while kiosks offer new Avengers-themed prizes like Collectible Power Cards.

Throughout the campaign, ‘DOOMHOUR’ will strike at random times, offering customers double tickets on any green swipe games. D&B Rewards members will get a 24-hour heads up about the DOOMHOUR, while the rest of us peasants will simply have to wait for the alarm to blare. Registered members will also get access to new Rewards Challenges throughout the campaign.

Of course, Dave and Buster’s bars are also now serving a spread of Doom-themed drinks. For the alcohol-inclined, D&B offers the Doomsday's Dominion, Multiversal Mule, and Fantastic Flight. New mocktails include Panther's Potion and Captain’s Punch.

Marvel has been collaborating with everything from KFC to the MLB in the lead-up to Avengers: Doomsday, releasing in theaters on December 18. Dave & Buster’s, however, appears particularly willing to commit to the bit, which is exactly what Disney execs are looking for.

"Rather than creating a traditional promotion, they transformed their entire business into an immersive celebration of Marvel Studios' Avengers: Doomsday," said Lylle Breier, EVP of Partnerships, Promotions and Events at The Walt Disney Studios. "The result is a bold, fan-first experience that extends the story beyond the theater and into the real world in a way only Dave & Buster's could."

articles.title: Bill Skarsgård Explains Why Starring in Hideo Kojima’s Physint Is a ‘Big Deal’ for Him
articles.summary: Skarsgård opened up about Physint in a November 5 episode of Josh Horowitz’s Happy Sad Confused podcast, where he revealed that he’s a massive fan of the Metal Gear series and shared a conversation he had with Kojima regarding his love for cinema.
articles.body:
In September 2026, Hollywood’s resident horror icon Bill Skarsgård was confirmed to play the lead role in Hideo Kojima’s highly anticipated action-espionage project Physint .

This game marks a long-awaited return to form from Kojima as fans pine for another Metal Gear-style experience. And while much about it is still unknown, we got just a smidge more information about the project thanks to its leading man, Bill Skarsgård.

Skarsgård opened up about the game in a November 5 episode of Josh Horowitz’s Happy Sad Confused podcast, where he revealed that he’s a massive fan of the Metal Gear series and shared a conversation he had with Kojima regarding his love for cinema.

“That’s a big deal for me,” he said. “Specifically, the Metal Gear Solid games. I played every single [one], at least the ones on [console] platform. Starting from the one on PlayStation 1 all the way to the last one. I was very enamored by [Kojima], the mythology and the universes he creates, but also the sort of mystique and allure about him, as well.

“I was really into it growing up. He is an auteur, but he’s a video game auteur. He’s fluent in filmmaking, and film, and cinema. I think at this point, I remember at one point way back, 20 years ago, there was talk of a Metal Gear solid movie. ‘Is Hideo going to direct it? Of course, I can’t wait to see him transition into film.’ I asked him, ‘Would you ever do a film?’ and he’s like, ‘No.’ At this point, what he’s doing is inventing a new medium. It is film. It’s eight hours worth of narrative, but it’s also an entire universe that you play. It truly is, quite literally, worldbuilding. Now, with technology, we’re getting closer and closer to something that's photorealistic and interactive when you play it. He’s a pioneer, and he keeps going out to untreaded waters.”

Skarsgård went on to confirm that he is providing performance capture for the game, something he already has experience with thanks to his role in Marvel’s Eternals and his extensive past working with mocap studio Goodbye Kansas (known for Alan Wake 2, God of War, Cyberpunk 2077 and many more).

This is the latest glimpse into the game we’ve gotten since the cast was revealed in September, which also includes Charlee Fraser, Don Lee, and Minami Hamabe. And in early October, Kojima discussed Physint in a podcast, saying he wants the project to “evoke the roots of Metal Gear Solid games” but be a “new interactive experience with a different kind of spy action,” as told by IGN’s Ryan McCaffrey .

Most notably, Physint recently changed hands from Sony to Xbox ; in a bombshell statement, Kojima said the game faced cancellation from the PlayStation parent company, but luckily, Microsoft stepped in to keep it alive. Sources told Bloomberg the project "missed deadlines and was on track to be well over budget despite being years away from release," suggesting that PlayStation’s seemingly sudden decision to drop the game was a direct result of these issues.

For now, fans can look forward to the Death Stranding anime , as well as watch out for more from Kojima’s upcoming horror game, OD Knock , starring Hunter Schafer and Sophia Lillis. News on the Metal Gear movie continues to be sparse, with its last big update happening earlier this year when Final Destination: Bloodlines duo Zach Lipovsky and Adam B. Stein were brought on to direct .

Image Credit: Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images for BAFTA

articles.title: Forest Temple Dungeon Walkthrough - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains
articles.body:
Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains the same, there's plenty of new differences to be found while exploring Hyrule. Seven years have passed since Link pulled the Master Sword free, and now seeks an old friend deep within the Forest Temple that has been corrupted by Ganondorf's influence.

Meeting with Sheik, Link learns a new melody to return to the Sacred Grove at any time, and with his new trusty Hookshot, ascends to the entrance of the temple to find a Sage and the Forest Medallion they keep.

As you enter the strange temple, it seems more like a manor overtaken by the greenery around it. You'll find a large entryway with a locked door, with giant trees flanking you on both sides.

No sooner than taking your first steps will two Wolfos appear to ambush you! You might be bigger, but that doesn't make these foes any less dangerous. Much like the Lizalfos, they'll alternate which one pursues while the other lurks in the background. Try to keep your eye on both while focusing on the present threat, and dodge backward away from their swipes to jump forward when their back is exposed, or charge up a spin attack!

Once the pair have been defeated, you'll notice the door in front of you is locked. Some people stash their front door key under a nearby rock, but the owners of the Forest Temple have opted for a different approach. Look up to the eastern side for a long wall of vines going up the massive tree, which will lead you to some high branches. You'll need to run along the long branch to the tree on the opposite side to find a small Treasure Chest with a Small Key inside!

While you're up here on the high trees that you climbed up via the vines, be sure to look back at the top of the vine wall on the eastern tree. Near the top past the branches you climbed up to is the first of several Gold Skulltulas, which you can defeat at a distance with your hookshot and claim its token.

Unlock the front door to head inside the temple proper, and defeat the large Skulltula who tries to block your way by slicing its backside.

Once in the main foyer of the Forest Temple, you'll find a large ornate lift around four colored torches. The residents of the Forest Temple will make themselves known - the Four Poe Sisters - and each will take one of the colored flames away, sealing the lift as they vanish with a laugh. Your objective will be to claim these fires back, which are now hidden across the temple grounds.

The foyer is divided up into several color-coded sections: Red windows to the left on the west, blue on the right to the east, and a green window straight ahead to the north, though several entrances are blocked or otherwise barred.

Before moving on, be sure to head straight ahead toward the green stained-glass window. As you move up the stairs, turn to the right to find a Gold Skulltula hiding on an inner wall by a blue window, and hit it with your Hookshot.

Head north through the door under the green stained-glass window, and into a hall with a new enemy. The Blue Bubble is a crazed flying skull protected by blue flames, and will try to ram into you. Hold your ground with shield raised, and the flames will douse as it bounces off, giving you the opportunity to quickly slice it apart or use your Hookshot.

As you enter the next room, the door will seal, pitting you against much more formidable foes: Stalfos.

These enemies are as patient as they are lethal. The only good news is that similar to Lizlafos and Wolfos, they'll respect the rules of engagement and face you one at a time, but can alternate who attacks. They are incredibly defensive foes, and trying to slash head-on will have little effect.

Instead, you'll want to become even more patient than your foes. Bait out their attacks, and watch their movements. Stalfos often employ a series of swings, slashing to the side twice before a delayed overhand hit. Get in a quick hit after the first two swings, then dodge out of the way of the last strike.

Be warned, as the Stalfos are lethal even at a distance. If you see one back up only for its blade to glint, be ready for a massive jump attack! Quickly strafe jump to the side, then launch your own strike before the skeleton can recover!

Once both foes are down, a new Small Treasure Chest will appear, holding another Small Key for you to move deeper into the temple.

Head back to the foyer, but don't use it on the red door just yet. Instead, turn your attention to the northwest, where a large blue block is in the way of a door on the lower floor. Play the Song of Time in front of the block, and it will disappear, letting you access the northwestern courtyard.

This large outdoor area is full of greenery, and a few lurking enemies like Deku Babas lying in wait, so be careful when exploring. A small island in the middle of a pond holds a large well, and off to the right you can spy a huge trail of vines crawling with Skullwalltulas trailing all the way up to a distant balcony.

First things first, head over to the trail of vines and use your Hookshot to eliminate the Skullwalltulas cluttering up the path before ascending to the first floor balcony yourself. The passage has crumbled close, but there's another balcony to the north, with a target you can latch onto using your Hookshot.

Zip across and explore this section to find a switch. Stepping on it will lower the water in the large well below, allowing you dive down into it.

Take a leap into the well to land in the shallower water, revealing a path to the northeast courtyard. Along this basement trail, you'll also find another Small Treasure Chest with your third Small Key!

Climb up the ladder here into the other courtyard, which has a few different features. Octoroks lurk in a small moat here that you'll want to deflect their projectiles first, and then look for a target to Hookshot across the water to find a large Treasure Chest, which holds the Dungeon Map!

There's a block above you that prevents going higher, so return to the other side of the moat and go through the door to return to the foyer, stepping on a switch to unlock the gate on the blue side of the room.

Now armed with two keys, use one of them on the eastern red door. Defeat the Blue Bubble in the hallway to enter the next large room.

In this large room to the east that spans multiple stories, the first thing you may notice is a spotlight above your head. Soon, the shadow beneath you will grow to reveal the shape of a hand, and the moment the spotlight turns from blue to red, quickly dash away to avoid an incoming Wallmaster!

These large hands will try and grab you if you remain unaware or preoccupied. If you get grabbed, you'll only have a moment to try to break free before the Wallmaster yanks you upward to warp you back to the entrance to the Forest Temple!

Instead, dodge out of the way as it lands, then quickly lunge in with a sword slice before the Wallmaster can retreat, and it will trouble you no more in this room.

With the threats out of the way, turn your attention to the nearby ladder, and climb up to find a series of corridor passages. Looking along the floor, you can spot yellow arrows pointing to the south, and they are coming from a large stone block to the west. Run around the corner and along a balcony to get to the other side of the block, then push it east and then south, before going around back along the balcony to push it west until it sits down in a recessed slot.

If you try to climb up here to the second floor, you'll find a similar narrow passage with another stone block, but there's not enough room to pull it back. Instead, return to where you first pushed the block on the lower level, and you'll find that it revealed a ladder up to another part of the second floor, putting you on the other side of the stone block.

Push the block to the south until it won't move, then return back downstairs and take the other ledge back up so that you can continue to push the block east until it also falls into a small recess, allowing you to climb upward to floor 3F.

This path leads to another large room with a new locked door, and a strange eye target above in a twisted frame. There are also a few smaller floating Blue Bubbles here, and you can snipe them out of the sky with your Hookshot to douse their flames before running in to finish them off.

Before unlocking the door to the north, be sure to look west for a switch, which will activate a lift, allowing you to quickly move up and down this large multi-story area (in case you forgot to explore the courtyard first and need to get that key).

Unlocking then next corridor will lead to a strange twisting path effecting not only the hallway, but the red chapel room beyond. All the floors, platforms, and balconies (even a large blue chest!) will have twisted to the left, meaning you'll need to hop along the tilted platforms instead of exploring the room normally. Beware of another Wallmaster, and quickly cross to a doorway leading east (if you fall down, there's a ladder to take you back up to the middle platform).

The next area is a long stairwell, with strange portraits placed across its floors. One will bear the resemblance of a certain Poe Sister you at the start of the dungeon, and it will run away to a different portrait when you draw close. Ignore the Poe for now, and head down to floor 2F to enter the far door.

In this arena, you'll be pitted against more Stalfos, with giant bubbling pit of toxic green ooze in the middle of the room! Spacing will be key here, as you'll want to both bait out the Stalfos attack, but leave them open on even ground that you can land your own attacks without taking damage. Leave space open to dodge toward the walls instead of dodging toward the pit in the middle.

Once you've defeated the first, two more will appear, and you'll need to move carefully to ensure you aren't flanked. Let them come to you on safe ground, rather than trying to advance on them into toxic territory.

When the next two Stalfos go down, a large Treasure Chest will appear as your reward. Be sure to look for pots around the room to heal up, and then claim your new ranged weapon -- the Fairy Bow!

Much like the Fairy Slingshot, this ranged weapon can hit all types of targets at a distance -- from enemies to eye switches, and even foes lurking in paintings...

One of the doors to the west is locked, so instead turn back east to find an eye target above the door, and unlock it to return to the previous room.

Now you'll be able to use your Fairy Bow to snipe the portraits that the Poe sister appears in from afar: on both side of the 2F Floor landing, and at the top of the 3F Floor stairwell.

When all three portraits have been shot down, the ghost will have no choice but to appear at the bottom of the room. Jo, is the second born of the four Poe Sisters, and she moves similarly to other Poes, but hits harder.

If you try to target her directly, she'll often turn invisible, and swing her torch around to deal a lot of damage if you don't strafe the charge attack. This spinning charge will leave her dizzy for a moment, allowing you to quickly step in and get some attacks off before she vanishes.

Repeat the assault after her next spin attack, and Jo will go down, releasing the red flame she carried in her torch, which will unlock a new small Treasure Chest holding the next Small Key.

With a new key, head to other side of the central room you got the Fairy Bow in, and enter the blue wing of the manor. It's nearly identical to the other side, including the same portraits showing a blue ghost this time.

Repeat the process of sniping the portraits from afar on the second and third floor landings to force the next Poe Sister out of hiding. Beth, the third born, is a nearly identical fight.

Watch for the spinning attacks and dodge around them, waiting for Beth to get dizzy from the attack so you can run in and slash her to pieces.

When the second Poe Sister goes down, her blue flame will be yours, unlocking a large Treasure Chest that holds the Compass!

Looking at the map now with the compass, you'll find that even though the blue and red wings of the temple mirror each other pretty closely, there's a locked door up on floor 3F past where you defeated Beth, so you'll need to find a key elsewhere if you want to continue on that path.

Remember that strange twisting frame with the eye switch around the twisted hallway you took to get here?

Retrace your steps to the east, back down through the red wing and twisted red chapel, along the twisted hallway and back outside. Shoot the eye up here, and it will "straighten" the next hallway, moving the room back into its original position too!

Before entering, return back to the multi-story room nearby with all the stone blocks you had to push. Drop down to floor 2F and move along the yellow arrows you pushed the stone block along to a small balcony in the northeast corner. There's another eye switch here you can hit with your bow, causing a small Treasure Chest to drop down holding a Purple Rupee!

Going back through the untwisted red hallway, the red chapel room now has a hole in the middle of the bottom floor. More importantly, there's a stunning blue Treasure Chest next to it, and opening it will reveal the Boss Key -- the special key you'll need to access the boss of this dungeon!

Drop into the hole by the chest you just opened to fall down to floor 1F, and get out of the pool quickly to deal with some Blue Bubbles.

When you exit out to the south, you'll find yourself on a low balcony overlooking the northwest outdoor courtyard, but you don't want to jump down just yet.

When overlooking the northwest courtyard from the balcony you arrived on from floor 2F, look for a doorway to the south. There's a small ledge wrapping around to the side of the door, and if you follow it, you'll find a Gold Skulltula hiding along the wall just past it in reach of your Hookshot from this angle.

Enter the room to the west to get sealed in with a Floormaster. Unlike Wallmasters, these giant hands are far more aggressive, sprouting damaging green flames as they attempt to strike you. Just like the Bubbles, use your shield and stand firm to stun the fires out of them or evade their strike and wait for the flames to diminish before striking.

When a Floormaster is killed, three smaller forms will sprout from it. You'll need to act quickly and slice them all apart -- if they cling onto you and sap your health, they can gain enough power to reform into the larger Floormaster once again! Try using Din's Fire to quickly clear the room. This will spawn a small Treasure Chest holding a new Small Key!

Head through the southern door to find a shortcut back up to floor 3F, and hit the eye target to twist the red hallway and red chapel once again. This way, you can head back through the corridors to the blue wing of the manor, now that you have a key to unlock the door on the top floor of the stairwell where you defeated the Po Sister, Beth.

Head through the blue chapel and up a ladder to go down a hallway with some floating Green Bubbles you can snipe from a distance, then unlock the far door.

You'll be in a strange frigid room now, and much like the western side there is a eye target above the door in a frame, but it's frozen solid! To uncover this puzzle, step on a nearby switch to light a torch, then aim your bow so that the arrow passes through the flame and melts the ice around the eye, and it will twist the blue hallway!

With the blue chapel also twisted, you'll find a pit leading down to floor 1F that mirrors the other side of the temple. This leads to a long room with a trap falling from the ceiling.

Now that you've fallen down into the northeast corner of floor 1F, look for a side door leading back out onto the outdoor courtyard, where you can push a stone block to create a shortcut. If you turn around and look up at a strange gust of straw.

If you went back to the scarecrows in Lake Hylia after becoming an adult and played their song again, you'll have learned the Scarecrow's Song. Playing it here will cause Pierre to appear, which you can now hookshot over to, and you'll find a Gold Skulltula with him.

Return to the previous room and watch the falling ceiling tiles, noting the checkerboard design. There are also rays of light coming from some of the ceiling tiles where the trap does not fall, and that will be your guide.

Move between the rays of light when the trap moves upward, but watch out for shadows in the light that denote a Skulltula waiting to drop down an ambush you. Act quickly to stab them or move past them to the right where a switch under the light can be pressed to open the far door.

Carefully make your way forward, and note the two rays of light marking a safe spot in front of a small Treasure Chest holding 5 Arrows, and then make for the door.

The room beyond is an interesting one: There's a large block in the middle of the room with a painting over the top, mirroring one against the wall where a third green Poe Sister is hiding.

Shoot the Poe with your bow and she'll move to the block painting, jumbling it up into pieces. To force her out of hiding, you'll need to slide the block puzzle into place to reform her body.

Note that she'll try to trick you by adding a fifth block that has no place in the full puzzle. Disregard the part of her head with a darkened tassel on the top of the hood (it's the only one that doesn't occasionally move on its own), and use the lighter-colored piece as the top right corner of the block puzzle.

When it's fully formed, Amy, the fourth born of the Poe Sisters, will start to fight. She's stronger than her other sisters, and can spin at you multiple times in a row before getting dizzy and stopping her attack, so watch her movements carefully before moving in and striking.

Don't get too greedy, and keep outpacing the attacks until she reveals herself to be dazed. Once she's defeated, her green fire will be unlocked, and open the nearby door leading back to the foyer.

In the hall beyond, a large portrait of the fourth and final Poe Sister will block your path. Stay near the doorway and shoot when she comes into frame. She'll flee back into the foyer, only to realize her fellow sisters are all gone...

Chase after the weeping purple Poe to draw her into a fight, but Meg, the firstborn, will even the odds by summoning three other copies of herself to throw you off!

Your attacks have no effect on the fake versions, so you'll need to remain calm and act carefully. One of these Poes is not the same -- after all, she's the purple Poe, and should be carrying the right color torch. Wait until the correct Poe circles in front of you to pull out your bow and fire away! This will stun her, allowing you to follow up with several sword swings before she can vanish again.

When she appears a second time, her clones will have gotten wise and ditched the green flame... but she's still giving herself away. Look for the one Poe that has a lit torch, and fire away again.

For her third and final act, all of her clones will now have purple flame torches, making it harder to spot the real one. Be patient and watch them closely for a tell: all of her clones have narrowed eyes, but the real one's mask has wider eyes! Take one final shot at the real Poe to end Meg's reign of terror.

With all four Poe Sisters defeated, the torches will be lit once more, activating the lift to the basement B2.

Upon arriving, you'll find an odd room. The map points to a hall to the boss to the north, and smaller alcoves in many sections of the circular room, but the way forward is sealed except for some small windows. Instead, you'll need to use the large handholds built into the walls to push forward, rotating which sections the walls are blocking.

Before you start rotating the walls in the basement of the temple, look for an open doorway to the south. Be ready for a Skulltula to try and ambush you, and after taking it out, look inside the alcoves inner walls for a Gold Skulltula hiding out of view.

Note the gate with the hole leading a frozen eye switch to the east. You'll need to find some way to melt that ice, so start by pushing the handholds counter-clockwise.

This will move the open doorway to the northwest, revealing a switch you can step on. A torch in one of the small windows along the wall will light up, giving you something to melt that ice with!

Keep pushing the handholds further counter-clockwise, stopping once to enter the alcove in the southwest to find a Treasure Chest with 5 arrows, and then again when the window with the lit torch is in front of the room with the frozen eye.

Shoot an arrow through to melt it, and hit the eye to open the gate north to the boss door, which your Boss Key will now open. It's time to face whoever is responsible for this temple's corruption...

The Evil Spirit from Beyond, Phantom Ganon is a terrfiying clone of Ganondorf, and seems intent on destroying the Hero of Time here and now. Atop his dread steed, this incarnation of Ganondorf wields a massive spear imbued with lightning!

When the battle begins, Phantom Ganon will take off into one of the six identical paintings that ring this arena. When he returns, he won't be alone! Borrowing a trick from the Poe Sisters, he'll have fake copies also riding up through the paintings to keep you guessing.

When they reach the edge of the painting, the clones will turn back, as the real Phantom Ganon will leap through the painting. If you aren't quick enough to pin down the real one, he'll soar over the arena and slash down this his lightning spear, sending shockwaves of light across the floor that can be tough to dodge.

While you can try to line up Phantom Ganon and his clone to see which one turns back at the last second, there's another way to spot the fakes, though it's a lot less visible than Meg's clones:

If you remember at the start of the fight, Phantom Ganon was wielding his spear in his right hand. His clones however, will be holding the spear in their left hand, showing on the right side of the painting as you watch them approach. Focus instead only on the one holding his spear out to the left side of the painting, and fire away when he draws close.

After getting a few shots with your Fairy Bow in, Phantom Ganon will start getting more clever, adding a second, and then third clone to keep you swiveling. The trick for spotting the fakes still stands, but you'll need to pan the camera quickly to zero in on which one is the real Phantom Ganon before firing your bow.

Once you've hit him around 2-3 times with your bow, Phantom Ganon will leave his horse behind, signaling phase two of this fight. He'll instead opt to float high ahove you, doing away with his clones for a 1 v 1 fight!

Wreathed in green energy, he'll be invulnerable to any ranged attacks you might possess, so instead you'll need to get creative. After a moment, Phantom Ganon will summon a green magic orbs and slam it toward you with his spear.

You can slash your own sword when the orb draws near to send it back to Phantom Ganon imbuing the orb with light from the Master Sword. When he holds his spear up high for a big slash, he'll send it back quicker. You'll need to be just as quick, and get the orb back in his face before he can recover from the swing. This will stun him with his own energy blast, and he'll fall to the ground in a weakened state.

Race on over to his position as he falls to hit him with jump attacks and spin attacks to maximize your damage until he can recover, and then pull back to wait for his next move.

After a few successful rallies, Phantom Ganon may decide to trick you, floating around and then suddenly launching into a dive attack instead of tossing a projectile, and you'll need to react quickly to dodge!

The rallies you'll need to complete to hit the orb back and forth will become more prolonged, but hold your ground and find a steady rhythm to hit the attacks back. Once he falls for a third time, you'll be able to finish him off with another assault from the Master Sword.

The battle may be won, but the true Ganondorf seems unfazed by his minion's pathetic display.

He'll give Link a dire warning should they ever cross blades before his voice fades away, leaving you with a new Heart Container.

As with the other dungeons, you can step into the blue light to be transported out. This time however, you'll return to the Chamber of Sages first to finally meet the Sage of the Forest: Your childhood friend Saria. Thanks to your triumph in the temple, Saria has awoken as a Sage, and can now aid you in the fight against evil. Your reunion will be bittersweet, as her new duty will keep her in this chamber to imprison Ganondorf when the time comes, but before you go, she'll impart to you the Forest Medallion, so that you may carry her resolve with you, always.

Upon returning to the forest, you'll find yourself back in front of the Great Deku Tree. And amazingly, you'll be introduced to a tiny little fellow known as the Deku Tree Sprout! It seems that now that the evil has been beaten back from the forest, Kokiri will know relative peace, and a new Deku Tree will begin to take root. You'll also learn some important details about Link's past, and why it is that he's the only one to have grown in these last seven years.

You can now return to Kokiri Forest and talk to all of your old friends (though most still don't really realize you're actually Link from all those years ago).

Navi will suggest you return to Sheik back at the Temple of Time to update the Sheikah warrior on what's happened in the Forest Temple.

When you meet again, Sheik will have a new melody for you to learn:

This is the Prelude of Light, and like the Minuet of the Forest, you'll now be able to teleport back to the Temple of Time whenever you wish.

This is doubly fortunate, as you're now able to return to the Master Sword to its pedestal to return to the past as a child whenever you wish. Who knows, it just might be useful to do a bit of time-traveling now and again, you never know what might be affected across time...
