articles.title: Rat Ranching Guide - Probably Stolen Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Rat Ranching is not an easy process to work through in Probably Stolen. You'll be taking care of a small colony of rats, cutting them up, and then selling
articles.body:
Rat Ranching is not an easy process to work through in Probably Stolen. You'll be taking care of a small colony of rats, cutting them up, and then selling their meat to the public for a high profit. Food is one of the most lucrative trades you can work in, but getting to that point takes time, and there are critical things you need to know about taking care of rats. In this guide, we're going to cover everything you need to know about Rat Ranching and how to best get started with it in Probably Stolen.

How Rat Ranching Works in Probably Stolen

You can choose to begin Rat Ranching by purchasing it as a special upgrade from Joe Wild, or make it your starting profession at the beginning of the game. Buying it from Joe costs 750 Credits . You'll receive a starter's kit for taking care of rats, beginning with a small family of rats, an Animal Cage, a Livestock Feed Dispenser to put into the cage, and some food.

Contain all of your rats inside the Animal Cage, with the Livestock Feed Dispenser on the left side. You can place any type of food that you purchase from other characters into the dispenser, grind it up, and it automatically gives the rats food when they're hungry. The best kinds of food you can put into the dispenser are going to be: Nutrifruit, Milk, Peat, and Cheese .

You want to avoid any type of rat meat. If you give rats the meat you cut up after butchering them, their health deteriorates, and they have a higher chance of becoming diseased.

Expect your rat family to begin growing up in a short amount of time. When a female rat becomes pregnant, she'll be in this state for three days before giving birth to children. Eventually, when a rat dies, you'll need to cut them up using a butcher knife, or you can buy an Auto Butcher and set it to do it automatically for you whenever a rat carcass is in the Animal Cage. You can then sell the meat you get from cutting up the rats to customers and make a profit.

Those are the basics of how Rat Ranching works. It's a bit more complicated than that, as you have to factor in the Animal Cage, the stats of your rats, breeding them, and making sure you don't keep diseased rats in the Animal Cage for long.

Your rats will remain in the Animal Cage, and that's where they're also going to expand. As the females become pregnant, more rats begin to take up the cage. You'll have to expand it using Metal Ingots from a furnace. You can do this five times to expand the various rows and prevent Overcrowding, a negative buff that all rats get when they're stuck inside a cage without too much room (which does happen often).

A good way to help out with this is to manually choose which rats to place into your Auto Butcher, even if they're not dead. Getting a second Animal Cage is also a good idea, but you'll need a second food dispenser to feed both of them.

Additionally, as time goes by, the durability of the Animal Cage goes down. When this happens, at night, some of the rats get out and appear in other parts of your shop. They can show up in the display case, your base inventory, your counter, or even in other containers. They'll also leave behind Rat Feces when they do this. You'll need to repair an Animal Cage using Metal Scraps.

As you get the Animal Cage in good quality and expand it, knowing what rats to keep and breed is also important too. Rats with higher stats live longer, meaning you can get more meat from them when you use your knife or Auto Butcher.

Whenever you hover over a rat, you'll get a breakdown of their stats. You can see it for every rat, including whether they're male or female, their age, health, hunger, hunger rate, expected litter (if they breed), and if they've reached maturity.

You'll always be able to see these base stats. However, if you buy the Gene Scanner from Dr. Jackson. It costs a hefty price, but you can see if these stats are positive or negative.

Rats with negative stats are ones you want to avoid having for too long in your Animal Cage. If they stay, there's a chance they might mate with your females, and their offspring rats also have these negative stats. You can use the Wire Cutters on any rat to neuter them, preventing them from mating with other rats in your colony.

At the start of each day, it helps to go through your rat colony and double-check that none of them have become diseased or are immunocompromised. If you see any rat with an immunocompromised status, remove them as quickly as possible or, at the very least, neuter them. You can also set the Auto Butcher to remove any rats that become sick or are a prion carrier.

The prion carrier is what rats get if they eat rat meat. If you're not feeding your rats that meat, you'll never see it, but it's possible you might purchase one from a retired Rat Rancher.

Eventually, most of your rat colony should have green positive stats. These provide you with the best rats that you can take care of and turn into food to sell for the best prices. I recommend waiting until a rat reaches its Elder stage (11 days old) before considering butchering them, as this yields the largest amounts of meat that you can sell for the most.

You can still use rats labeled as (Mature), but I don't recommend it if you're trying to yield the largest amount of meat every day.

articles.body:
Ice Arrows are an upgrade for the Fairy Bow in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This item lets you infuse your normal arrows with Ice, helping you deal extra damage and solve certain puzzles. This consumes 1 arrow and 1 bar of magic. They are not found in a major dungeon, so you may be wondering how to get the Ice Arrows.

See IGN's guide to Ice Arrows, including location and requirements, below.

Ice Arrows are found in the deepest cell of the Gerudo Proving Grounds. You will need to complete everything up to the Water Temple, then complete the Gerudo Fortress to get the Gerudo Pass and gain access to the Proving Ground. Technically some of the puzzles require the Silver Gauntlets, but you can avoid those and still get the Ice Arrow.

Enter the Proving Grounds (30 Rupee entry) then complete all of the rooms you are able to with your current items. Use the Lenses of Truth to spot hidden walls and secrets. Once you have 6 Small Keys, head back to the starting room and go straight ahead into the treasure room. Start unlocking the doors on the left.

As soon as your pass through the first key door, climb the chain wall next to the door to find a hidden room above with another Small Key inside. This brings our grand total to 7, enough to reach the Ice Arrows in the middle.

All you have to do is just keep opening doors on the left side until you reach the large chest in the center, containing the Ice Arrow.

articles.title: How to Get Phantom Blade Zero True Ending: Walkthrough and Requirements Checklist - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Phantom Blade Zero has more than one ending, and its True Ending has a long list of requirements. Essentially, you'll have to complete all side quests
articles.body:
Phantom Blade Zero has more than one ending, and its True Ending has a long list of requirements. Essentially, you'll have to complete all side quests (the purple ones), but beware that some of them have a specific order, and you won't be able to complete them if you progress too far in the main story. That's why this guide will show you how to get Phantom Blade Zero's True Ending with every step that you need to know.

As you make progress in the main story, it's important that you complete Secrets at the Heart of the Lake and Bloodline Awakening before you enter Mountain God Temple on Mount Soulrend.

Phantom Blade Zero True Ending Requirements and Checklist

As a summary, these are the steps that you need to achieve the True Ending:

Collect all six of Firefly’s Memory Flowers .

Use the three doors at Herald’s Illusion.

Use Puppet’s Tongue to open Crimson Manor .

Insert both Crystal Puppet Eyes into Puppet No. 99 .

Destroy the ritual and complete Secrets at the Heart of the Lake .

Complete all five Lóng Pillar trials and finish Bloodline Awakening .

Defeat the last series of bosses: Leng Tu, Herald of the Veil, Meng Hua, The Merciful Lady of the Blossom Veil , and Zuo Shang .

articles.title: How to Get the Biggoron Sword - Trading Sidequest - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Biggoron Sword is an optional Weapon obtained by completing a lengthy trading sequence in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. The Thread of Light,
articles.body:
Biggoron Sword is an optional Weapon obtained by completing a lengthy trading sequence in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. The Thread of Light, "From a Pocket Egg Comes...", involves Link receiving an item and having to bring it to someone else across Hyrule, sometimes on a tight timer. This page details how to get the Biggoron Sword, including the location of every trade, tips and tricks, and all prerequisites.

Find IGN's complete guide to the obtaining the Biggoron Sword below:

The Thread of Light, "From a Pocket Egg Comes..." can be started as soon as you become Adult Link, meaning you can get the Biggoron Sword before tackling a single Temple if you like. Alternatively, if you want to make things a little easier on yourself, start this quest after the Water Temple. This gets you the Longshot and reopens the Lake Hylia to Zora's Domain shortcut.

You will need to complete two other side activities beforehand:

Free King Zora from the Red Ice in Zora's Domain (requires doing most or all of Ice Cavern)

To begin the quest, speak to the Cucco Lady in Kakariko Village as Adult Link. She gives Link the Pocket Egg to begin with. At dawn, a Pocket Cucco will hatch from the egg. She encourages Link to bring the pocket cucco to a heavy sleeper. Playing the Sun’s Song to reach dawn will make the egg quickly hatch into the Pocket Cucco!

Once you have the Pocket Cucco, head to the two story house with the red roof directly ahead of the village entrance. Inside, in the bed under the stairs, is Talon, the owner of Lon Lon Ranch, once again fast asleep. Show him the Pocket Cucco to startle him awake. Once Talon is up, bring the Pocket Cucco back to the Cucco Lady, and she trade you a new Cucco, Cojiro.

Once you’ve obtained Cojiro the blue cucco, head to the Lost Woods in Kokiri Forest. From the Lost Woods entrance, take the very first left, and the Cucco Lady’s older brother is found sitting against the taller tree stump (where Skull Kid was found previously). He’s asleep, so show Cojiro to him to wake him up. He’ll deem Link a good person, and give you the next item in the sequence to bring back to Kakariko Village: an Odd Mushroom.

Once you obtain the Odd Mushroom, a timer for 4 minutes will appear at the top of the screen . This is the amount of time you have to bring the mushroom to Granny’s Cauldron in Kakariko Village. Warp songs like the Nocturne of Shadow will cancel out the timer and fail the quest, which Navi will even warn you about, so you'll have to find a different fast route.

You can pass through the Lost Woods, take the shortcut to Goron City ( right, left, then forward ), then descend into Kakariko Village down Death Mountain. Or, quickly exit the Lost Woods and Kokiri Forest into Hyrule Field, call Epona, and ride directly to Kakariko. Whichever you feel more comfortable with.

Once you enter Kakariko Village, enter the Potion Shop (upper north side of the Village, near the Death Mountain gate), then exit in the Potion Shop via the side door to the left of the counter to reach the backyard, and the entrance to Granny’s Cauldron. If it happens to be night time, you will need to grab a Cucco from the Cucco pen then jump over the metal gate in front of the Windmill to reach the backyard of the Potion Shop instead . Head inside, and give Granny the Odd Mushroom, and she’ll turn it into the next step in the sequence: the Odd Poultice.

Once Granny gives you the Odd Poultice, bring it back to her son in the Lost Woods. Thankfully, there’s no timer for this step, so you can take your time getting back, or use a warp song if you’d like. Regardless of your method, return to where you found the Master Craftman’s Son in the Lost Woods, and you’ll find Fado instead, with the man now missing. Speak to her, and she’ll reveal that he’s gone, but she wants the Odd Poultice since it was made from forest mushrooms. In return, she’ll give you the Poacher’s Saw.

The Poacher’s Saw seemingly belonged to the Master Craftsman’s Son, so you’ll have to bring it to the Master Craftsman. He’s found outside the Carpenter’s Tent in the Gerudo Valley. Unless you already did the Gerudo Fortress quest the bridge in Gerudo Valley will be out, but Epona can jump the gap with a running start. Show the Poacher's Saw to the Master Craftsman and he will give you the Broken Goron Sword.

The Broken Goron’s Sword must be brought to Biggoron, found at the top of Death Mountain. Whether you warp to Death Mountain Crater using the Bolero of Fire, or climb up Death Mountain Trail, carefully make your way up to the peak, just outside the summit and Great Fairy Fountain. Biggoron is found across from the fountain, rubbing his eyes. Show him the Broken Goron’s Sword, and he’ll take it off your hands in exchange for getting his eye drops from King Zora. So he’ll give you the Prescription to bring to King Zora.

Once you have the Prescription, head to Zora’s Domain. If you haven’t already freed King Zora from the red ice using Blue Fire, you’ll have to do so in order to talk with him. Blue Fire is found in the Ice Cavern, but can also be purchased from the Potion Shop in Kakariko Village. Anyway, show King Zora the Prescription, and he’ll give you the key ingredient to make the eye drops: the Eyeball Frog.

Once you receive the Eyeball Frog from King Zora, a timer for two and a half minutes will appear at the top of the screen . You’ll only have this long to bring the eyeball frog to the scientist at the Lakeside Laboratory at Lake Hylia. Once again, since there’s a timer, warp songs won’t work. Our recommended route is taking the Zora River to Lost Woods shortcut, which is found just outside Zora's Domain on the left. Exit the Woods into Hyrule Field, then quickly call and ride Epona over to Lake Hylia. Alternatively, if you have finished the Water Temple, you can exit Zora's Domain directly to Lake Hylia.

Once you’re at Lake Hylia, head into the Lakeside Laboratory, and speak to the scientist. Give him the Eyeball Frog, and after he laments that he won’t be able to eat it, he’ll make the Specialty Eye Drops for Biggoron.

Once the Scientist makes the Specialty Eye Drops for you, a timer will once again appear up top, just like with the Eyeball Frog. This time, for 3 and a half minutes. And, like the previous timers, the warp songs cannot be used here, so you’ll have to find another fast way to Death Mountain Peak.

Three minutes is plenty of time to just take the most direct route. Exit the Laboratory and hop on Epona, then ride across Hyrule Field to Kakariko Village, then Death Mountain. Head up the mountain as fast as you can. Careful of the raining fire and spiders in the final section of Death Mountain. If you don't run into any major issues you should have about 30-45 seconds to spare. Once again, if you are past Water Temple you can instead take a series of shortcuts: Lake Hylia to Zora's Domain, Zora's Domain to Lost Woods via Zora River, Lost Woods to Goron City, Goron City to Death Mountain.

Give the Eye Drops to Biggoron. After he celebrates finally being able to see, he’ll give you the Biggoron Receipt.

Once you obtain the receipt for the Biggoron Sword, you’ll have to wait three days before the sword is ready. So pull out that Ocarina, and play Sun’s Song repeatedly until three days have passed. If you lose track of how much time has passed, talk with Biggoron and he’ll tell you how much longer until it’s ready.

Once three days have passed, speak to Biggoron, and give him the receipt. He’ll give you the Biggoron Sword.

articles.title: Wanted List Guide: Who to Report, Consequences, Threats, and More - Probably Stolen Guide - IGN
articles.summary: You'll receive a Wanted List within the first few days of starting your run in Probably Stolen. It's from the Security at the station, and they want
articles.body:
You'll receive a Wanted List within the first few days of starting your run in Probably Stolen . It's from the Security at the station, and they want you to notify them if you ever encounter any of the nine individuals shown on this list. Many of them don't use their own names, and you'll receive a reward for doing so. However, there are consequences for doing so, and the wanted individual also provides you with incentives not to do it. In this guide, we're going to break down everything you need to know about the Wanted List in Probably Stolen.

Here's a breakdown of the nine people you'll see on the Wanted List in Probably Stolen.

Arthur Lafleur is a member of the Revolution on the station. If you encounter him, he'll ask you to not call Security if you attempt to do so. However, if you do, you'll lose reputation with the Revolution, and you'll receive 100 Credits (the lowest amount on the Wanted List).

If you don't report him, and you increase your reputation with the Revolution as you play, he becomes a more frequent person who shows up. However, only if you attempt to report him once. He'll ask that you don't do that and tell you he has little to do with the current Revolution. If you let him go, he'll put in a good word for you. Of the factions, the Revolution can be the toughest to get high because of how many people you have to work through. For those who want to support the Revolution (as getting too low with them can lead to an ending), it's good to keep him around as he'll also bring you supplies that you can buy. You want to attempt to report him, but don't commit to it.

James Bailey is someone who wants to move contraband and weapons as much as possible. He's someone who will offer you various illegal items and have you move them around if you're willing to buy from him. If you don't and call Security on him, you'll receive 300 Credits as a reward.

The downside to calling Security on James is that the illegal contraband goes away. You'll have to rely on other contacts in the Black Market (if you're going down that path), and find others if you want to make money that way. Keeping James around is a good idea if you're going to have Odin. You can purchase items from James and then sell them back to Odin, giving you a good margin of buying low and selling high between these two parties.

John Smith is a regular person with an unfortunate name, and is mistaken for several other people. You can choose to call Security on him, but he says that he's already been mistaken for someone else four other times that week. If you go through with it, Security grabs him, and they pay you the 150 Credits. However, he later returns and says that he only wants to buy groceries. You can try to have him arrested again, and if he is, he returns to vandalize your shop, never to be seen again.

However, if you never have John Smith arrested at all, he continually shows up to buy food at least once a week. Given how often he appears, and how willing he is to buy food, never calling Security on John is a good idea. Plus, you don't get too many benefits from calling Security on him. It's better to have him as a customer in the long run. His budget increases every week.

Juan is someone who can appear to you with a massive amount of food at least once a week. He offers it at a discounted price. When he appears, you can threaten to report him, and he'll beg you not to do it, reminding you of how much food he's willing to offer. If you confirm with Security and get him arrested, you'll get 125 Credits.

The downside is you lose a reliable client who brings a lot of food to you. Juan regularly comes with rows of Peat, Pilk, and juice that you can buy at a lower price. For those who are working on Rat Ranching or have a fish farm, keeping Juan is great for feeding these animals without too much effort. It's good to note that Juan's food typically has Heat on it, so if you don't sell it fast, use it on your animals, or hide it in a Smuggler's Cargo Bay, a Security inspection will take it away.

Leroy is a person who comes around to 'inspect' your market stall during the day. He's dressed up like a member of the Security force, and wants to make an inspection. Regardless of what you have, he's going to steal from you. He's a character you want to call Security on immediately, and make sure he doesn't steal from you. You'll gain Security reputation for doing it.

Li Bei Wen is a chemical researcher who approaches you. He first says that he's been trying to share his drug with others, and wants to prove that it works. He asks for you to sell it, and informs you that it's a narcotic that's not as addictive. If you first see Li, you can choose to have him arrested. You'll receive 400 Credits for his capture, and he won't escape.

However, by not turning Li in, you can begin to work with him. After selling the drugs he gives you, he'll ask how they worked and say he needs more time to perfect the formula. He also needs help, and asks that you bring him Chemical supplies. He'll show up at least once a week asking for them. After he gets them, he'll disappear for a bit, but then reappear and show you his result. Plus, he tells you how to recreate the recipe, allowing you to begin making Nomore injectors.

Lou is an extremely unique case compared to the other characters on the Wanted List. Lou arrives during month two or three. When she does, she shares that she's looking for dangerous weapons, and admits that she's going to use it on a person that she's holding hostage. She also warns you about what would happen if you do call Security on her. You'll get a high amount of money for it: 1,500 Credits. However, she'll return, which is a good thing.

There's a questline you'll get by calling Security on Lou once. Then, she returns, and you start to learn more about her and what's motivating her. Although she is harming other people, you learn that many of them are bad, or even worse, than she is. You can only learn this by reporting her when she appears, so making sure to report her once is essential for this part.

Odin usually turns up a few days after you start playing Probably Stolen. He says for you to not call Security on him, and hands you a business card. If you do call Security on Odin, you'll lower your reputation with the Revolution, and you get 300 Credits.

However, if you don't, Odin becomes a valuable contact. If you ever need to increase your reputation with the Revolution, call him on his business card and you can trade him weapons, materials, crates, access cards; he'll take nearly any item you can't normally sell openly, and pays you a decent amount of money. He'll show up two days after you call, and you can call him again five days after your previous call. It's better to not call Security on Odin, and use him as a contact to exchange goods.

The Butcher can show up within your first month. He appears with a pile of meat, a bag, and some other odd items. He offers you sell you the meat, but it has no origin. If you do buy his items, you'll discover a note inside the bag from a scavenger who says someone has been following him.

Turns out, the Butcher was killing people in the Lower Levels and selling their meat back to everyone. Of all the people on the Wanted List, the Butcher is the best person to call Security on. You'll get 400 Credits for it, and you'll increase your reputation with the Lower Levels. Although the Butcher is arrested, he escapes custody a few weeks later. He prevents you from going outside at night if you don't take a gun with you, but if you can have the Underground Exchange take him out if you give them 500 Credits. It's worth it to get rid of the Butcher, and make sure he doesn't further hurt the Lower Level citizens.

articles.title: After Buying EA, Silver Lake and PIF Are Reportedly Now Seeking to Acquire Gaming Software Provider Unity
articles.summary: After Buying EA, Silver Lake and PIF Are Reportedly Now Seeking to Acquire Gaming Software Provider Unity
articles.body:
A consortium of investors including private equity firm Silver Lake Partners and Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund PIF has held recent talks to acquire gaming software provider Unity.

A Reuters report citing confidential sources familiar with the matter states that PIF and Silver Lake, the latter of which already owns 8% of Unity, approached the company in recent weeks. The buyer consortium discussed a valuation of about $25 billion before Unity’s latest earnings report, which lifted its market capitalization to roughly $21.5 billion.

Unity has reportedly been consulting with an investment bank to evaluate its options following the approach, however talks are preliminary and no deal is assured.

Should the acquisition go ahead, this would be another major investment into the games industry for Silver Lake and PIF. The two firms previously teamed up with Jared Kushner’s Affinity Partners to acquire Electronic Arts for $55 billion in a deal that was finalised in August . Since then the publisher has initiated major corporate restructurings and studio closures, most recently shutting development studio BioWare and cancelling the next Mass Effect game .

Unity’s popular game engine and development tools have been used to create thousands of mobile, console, and PC games. These include Genshin Impact, Hollow Knight, Among Us, Subnautica, and Beat Saber, to name just a few. Notably, Unity’s tools are also used by Scopely, the developer of Monopoly Go!, and Niantic, the maker of Pokemon Go, both of which are owned by a group that includes Silver Lake, PIF, and Affinity Partners.

Silver Lake has already invested $400 million into Unity and with its 8% stake it remains one of its largest shareholders. Since going public in 2020, Unity has expanded beyond its game engine business into advertising technology and broader real-time 3D software, and its tools are increasingly used in automotive design, filmmaking, architecture, and industrial simulation.

After news of the acquisition talks first broke, Unity shares rose nearly 15% in regular trading and sit at $48.80 per share at the time of writing.

Season 1 of Modern Warfare 4 has arrived, bringing with it countless balance adjustments, updates and general fixes to improve game balancing, performance, and stability.

This page acts as a comprehensive breakdown of the Season 1 Patch for MW4, including a link to the full Patch Notes.

The November 5 Patch consists of various fixes and improvements to both Multiplayer and DMZ modes.

Reduced maximum health in Hardcore modes from 30 to 22.

Fixed an exploit that allowed players to attach Proximity Mines to Seeker Drones.

Fixed an out-of-bounds exploit at Wolves Stadium in Combat Outpost.

Fixed an issue where the Cronen Osprey equipped with the Helix MK. II Apex Attachment could clip through the player during Finishing Moves.

Fixed an issue where Boksu Prime did not unlock after completing the Classic Prestige 10 Track.

Fixed an issue where the Mercurial Drift Multiplayer Weapon Mastery Camo remained locked after players completed its unlock requirements.

Added a Select/Deselect All option to the Edit Quickplay Modes menu in Multiplayer lobbies.

Fixed an issue in Kill Block 24/7 where the Loadout selection menu could overlap the map preview.

Fixed an animation issue with the reconfiguration transition on Kill Block.

Fixed an issue where the Damage Dealt display after death did not appear correctly in Private Match.

Fixed an issue where the second player in Splitscreen would be unable to access the View Maps tab.

Fixed a crash that could occur when the second player in Splitscreen attempted to generate a weapon using Gunny.

Fixed an issue in Inflation where the personal Cash counter could incorrectly double instead of reflecting the amount collected.

Fixed an issue where players could not use the Sedative Inhaler while holding a Knife.

Fixed an issue where the Free Prep Trait only provided Radiation Blockers instead of a random Consumable.

Fixed an issue with Colossus spawning at the Military Base before the Armory was opened.

Fixed an issue where players were unintentionally getting UAV pings when enemy UAVs were active.

Fixed an issue where Ammo Boxes could get stuck inside of vehicle doors when thrown against them.

Fixed an issue where progress toward the High-Value Escort Calling Card Challenge was not tracking correctly.

Fixed an issue where certain DMZ Lieutenant Dog Tags did not count toward Camo Challenge progression.

Updated the Dog Tag Case to display the most recently acquired Dog Tags first.

Fixed an issue where DMZ Lieutenant targets could appear multiple times on the Boss Board, even after being eliminated.

Fixed an issue in DMZ Gunsmith where players could try to re-equip Attachments they no longer owned.

Fixed an issue where the DMZ Weapon Stash 1 upgrade remained available after completion, allowing players to try to purchase it again.

Fixed an issue where completed Orders displayed a low-resolution checkmark in the After Action Report.

Fixed an issue where the Bruen Field-OP Optic reticle did not match its preview when equipped on Pistols.

Fixed an issue where the XP Token menu prompt would not highlight when hovered over.

articles.title: Elon Musk Puts the Brakes on Cybertruck Production to Focus on Tesla's Cybercab, Disappointing Diehard Fans
articles.summary: Elon Musk has confirmed plans to "wind down" production of the Cybertruck at Tesla's gigafactory.
articles.body:
Elon Musk has confirmed plans to wind down production of the Cybertruck at Tesla's gigafactory in Texas.

“Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production,” Musk tweeted today .

Musk’s tweet left the door open to further production elsewhere, but Cybertruck lead engineer Wes Morrill then suggested that Cybertruck was being discontinued. “Cybertruck was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab,” he tweeted . “Thanks to everyone who contributed to making the future looking like the future. As well to the community of owners whose adventures I've enjoyed and will continue to follow.”

Tesla Cybertruck Official Release - Slideshow

The angular Cybertruck launched in 2023 to much fanfare, but sales have been poor. Indeed, the truck has suffered online ridicule ever since it was introduced in 2019, when Musk himself shattered its supposed unbreakable glass during a live demo.

Musk’s announcement was met with a mixture of mocking social media posts and mourning from Tesla devotees. “Did even last five years. Pathetic,” one person said. “It was already a bad enough day without this news. I need a second one!” another said.

In a tweet reply to one disappointed fan, Musk insisted the Cybertruck fleet “will be around for a long time.” Morrill replied to a fan who said they felt like "I lost a child" to say that Tesla would maintain spare parts and service support would continue.

Earlier this year, amid slow sales and tough questions about Cybertruck, Musk said it was "way more awesome than people realise." In April, the tech billionaire said Cybertruck was the "best product Tesla has ever made to date.”

The focus, now, is on Cybercab , which Musk has said will play a crucial role in Tesla’s robotaxi plans. According to Reuters , the two-seater robotaxi is still a small program, with production beginning only earlier this year. Tesla has listed an installed capacity of more than 125,000 units.
